answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by pricing identity. Before an agent may wander the market, it must lock a bond and collect vouches from staked peers. An attacker minting clones then pays one bond per fake identity and needs independent vouchers for each, so cost grows linearly with the attack. Clones cannot reuse a backer's vouch: it is tied to that stake, slashed if the newcomer defects. Forfeited bonds pile into a dune of lost capital, while honest agents treat the bonded registry as a haven where reputation outweighs the price of yet another fake account.
